name: Stockholm
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Stockholm: Nordic financial due diligence, arbitration support and research on listed and tech companies.
hero_lede: Investigative consulting for matters that run through Stockholm: Nordic banks and listed companies, technology and growth-stage businesses, disputes seated at the Stockholm arbitration institute or before the city's courts, and financial crime exposure in the Baltic Sea region. Scoped from Nashville with qualified Swedish professionals.
intro: Stockholm is Sweden's capital and largest city, with just under one million residents in the municipality and about 2.5 million in Stockholm County at the end of 2025. It is the seat of the government, the central authorities and the country's main financial institutions, and home to Nasdaq Stockholm, the principal Nordic equity market for many Swedish industrial, financial and technology groups. The city has a large technology and start-up sector, a concentration of banking, asset management and payments businesses, and professional services firms serving the wider Nordic and Baltic region. It is also a long-established seat for international commercial and investment arbitration, including East-West disputes.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Stockholm for several reasons. Investors and acquirers want due diligence on Swedish listed companies, private technology businesses and their founders and backers. Banks and payment firms with Baltic and Nordic operations face scrutiny over anti-money laundering controls, a theme made prominent by the cases arising from Swedish banks' Estonian business. Parties to arbitrations seated in Stockholm, often involving counterparties from Russia, Central Asia, Eastern Europe or China, need background research and asset information for enforcement. Public procurement, welfare-sector contracting and organised crime infiltration of legitimate business are further recurring concerns in the region.

matters.title: Due diligence on Nordic financial institutions
matters.text: Ownership, management, regulatory and litigation history of banks, payment institutions, fund managers and fintechs based in Stockholm, drawing on Bolagsverket filings, supervisory announcements, court decisions and media, for acquisitions, partnerships and correspondent or outsourcing relationships.

matters.title: Arbitration and award enforcement support
matters.text: Background research on opposing parties, witnesses and corporate groups in arbitrations seated in Stockholm, and lawful asset research to support recognition and enforcement of awards, frequently involving counterparties and assets outside Sweden, coordinated with counsel in each relevant jurisdiction.

matters.title: Technology and growth-company diligence
matters.text: Research on founders, investors, ownership structures and prior ventures of Stockholm technology and life sciences companies before investment, acquisition or partnership, including verification of claimed credentials, related-party relationships and disputes, using public registers and open sources.

matters.title: Baltic-linked AML exposure reviews
matters.text: Support to counsel and compliance teams examining customer, correspondent or ownership links between Stockholm institutions and the Baltic states, focusing on beneficial ownership chains, shell company indicators and adverse public records, without any access to supervisory or law enforcement data.

matters.title: Procurement and contractor integrity checks
matters.text: Background research on suppliers and subcontractors in public contracting, construction, welfare services and facilities management in the Stockholm region, looking for undisclosed ownership, phoenix company patterns, tax and payment remarks in public sources, and links to individuals with relevant convictions.

local_context.title: Stockholm District Court
local_context.text: Stockholm District Court, located in the Stockholm Court House on Kungsholmen, describes itself as Sweden's largest court, handling about 18,000 civil and criminal cases a year. Its district covers central Stockholm and Lidingö, while the suburbs fall under neighbouring district courts. Appeals go to the Svea Court of Appeal. Swedish court judgments and many case files are public documents, which makes litigation research comparatively productive.

local_context.title: Svea Court of Appeal
local_context.text: The Svea Court of Appeal in Stockholm hears appeals from courts in the capital region and is where high-profile financial crime cases are often decided. In September 2024 it convicted the former chief executive of Swedbank of gross swindling over statements about anti-money laundering in the bank's Estonian operations; Sweden's Supreme Court overturned that conviction in April 2026. The case illustrates how disclosure and AML questions reach Stockholm's courts.

local_context.title: Stockholm arbitration
local_context.text: The Arbitration Institute of the Stockholm Chamber of Commerce administers commercial and investment treaty arbitrations, and Stockholm has a long tradition as a neutral seat for disputes between Western and Eastern European, Russian and Chinese parties. Challenges to awards are heard by the Svea Court of Appeal. Arbitral proceedings are confidential, so background and asset research relies on public records in each relevant jurisdiction.

local_context.title: Supervisors and registers
local_context.text: Finansinspektionen, the Swedish financial supervisor, is based in Stockholm and publishes authorisations, sanctions and warnings about unauthorised firms. Company records held by Bolagsverket are covered on the Sweden country page. Swedish public access to official documents means that many authority decisions can be requested, but supervisory secrecy and tax secrecy still apply to much of what investigators would want to see.

tdsc_approach: For matters touching Stockholm, TDSC begins by mapping what Swedish public access law makes available, since court files, authority decisions and many filings can be requested, and then defines what must come from other jurisdictions, such as Baltic subsidiaries or the home country of an arbitration counterparty. Research draws on Bolagsverket records, court judgments, Finansinspektionen publications and open sources in Swedish and English, reviewed under the GDPR and Swedish data protection rules. For arbitrations, TDSC aligns work with counsel and with the confidentiality of the proceedings. Where interviews or local inquiries in Stockholm are needed, TDSC coordinates qualified Swedish professionals operating within Swedish law. TDSC has no office in Stockholm.

faqs.q: Are Swedish court records available for background research?
faqs.a: Largely, yes. Under Sweden's principle of public access to official documents, judgments and many case documents can be requested from courts such as Stockholm District Court and the Svea Court of Appeal, subject to secrecy rules. TDSC uses these requests lawfully and records what was obtained, and any personal data is limited to the agreed purpose.

faqs.q: Can TDSC support an arbitration seated in Stockholm?
faqs.a: Yes, as a consultant to counsel. TDSC researches opposing parties, corporate groups, witnesses and assets for arbitrations administered by the Stockholm Chamber of Commerce institute or seated in Stockholm. Proceedings are confidential, so TDSC works only from public and lawfully obtained records and coordinates with counsel in jurisdictions where enforcement may be sought.

faqs.q: Can TDSC obtain information from Finansinspektionen about a firm?
faqs.a: TDSC uses what Finansinspektionen publishes, including registers of authorised firms, sanctions decisions and warnings about unauthorised activity. Supervisory files are generally covered by secrecy and are not accessible to investigators. Requests for official documents that may be disclosable are handled transparently and, where appropriate, through the client's Swedish counsel.

faqs.q: Why do Stockholm due diligence matters often involve the Baltic states?
faqs.a: Large Swedish banking groups built significant operations in Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania, and AML failures in that region led to major investigations and litigation in Stockholm. Counterparty research on Stockholm institutions or their customers therefore often needs to extend to Baltic registers, courts and media, which TDSC addresses with research in those jurisdictions.

faqs.q: Does TDSC have staff in Stockholm?
faqs.a: No. TDSC has no office, staff or address in Stockholm or elsewhere in Sweden. Engagements are scoped and managed from Nashville. Where a matter needs local inquiries, TDSC coordinates independent Swedish professionals and works with the client's Swedish counsel, within a written scope agreed before work begins.
